findings.title: exprBorrowed does not walk several carrier shapes, so rule B is bypassed: a borrow laundered through a local copy / struct literal / deref copy is stored into a global and read after the target dies
findings.why: Rule B (checkStoreEscape:1438) refuses to store a *borrowed* value into a depth-0 place; it asks exprBorrowed(). exprBorrowed only answers true when the value's root binding has depth==0 (a parameter), so a local binding that merely *holds* a borrow is not borrowed: `var q: slice<u8> = p` has root depth 1 -> false. The same hole exists for every expression kind that is not in the switch and falls to `default: return false` (line 698): EX_STRUCTLIT, EX_DEREF, EX_ARRAYLIT, EX_CONV, EX_TRY, EX_LAMBDA. The depth check cannot compensate, because the value's recorded depth legitimately is 0 (`q`'s refDepth is inherited from the parameter), and in the struct-literal case exprRefDepth walks the fields and also finds 0. The invariant that is violated is the one stated in the file's own header comment: 'A borrowed value may not be stored where it outlives the call'. The effect summary does not compensate either: the store to a global is not recorded in any mask (EXTC_DUMP_EFFECTS shows toParam/toHome/other all 0x0 for the callee), so no call-site check exists.
findings.trigger: A function that stores a value derived from a parameter into a global (or a global's field/element), where the derivation is (a) a local copy `var q = p; G = q`, (b) an aggregate constructor `G = holder { p: p }`, (c) a copy through a dereference `G = *h`, or (d) an index/slice of a temporary `G = [p,p][0]`. The caller passes a view/ref into a nested block, so the global outlives the storage it ends up pointing at. The direct form `G = p` and `G.p = p` are correctly rejected.
findings.repro: Files in /tmp/rev/repro. (a) b3.extc: `var G: slice<u8> = "hi"` (global); `fn stash(p: slice<u8>) { var q: slice<u8> = p  G = q }`; main fills a block-local `[16]u8` with 'A'+i, calls stash(a[..]), then a sibling block creates the same `[16]u8` full of 90 and prints. `./build/extc b3.extc -o b3.c && gcc -fwrapv -O1 -o b3 b3.c && ./b3` -> `G = ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ` (expected: the block-local view must be rejected; cf. b0.extc, the same program with `G = p`, which is rejected with 'cannot store a borrowed value into something that outlives this call'). (b) d1.extc: `struct holder { p: ?ref i32 }`, `var G: holder = holder { p: null }`, `fn stash(p: ref i32) { G = holder { p: p } }`, caller passes `ref x` with `x` in a block; the emitted C compiles and `./d1` exits 70 (it read the reused stack slot; 103 was expected). d1b.extc, the same store written `G.p = p`, is rejected. (c) e1.extc: `fn stash(h: ref holder) { G = *h }` -> accepted, exit 70. (d) f2.extc: `G = [p, p][0]` -> accepted, prints an empty view.

findings.title: checkStoreEscape's `needsHome` early return lets any function that has a home arena store a borrowed reference into a global
findings.why: The justification covers only destinations whose lifetime is the home arena. When the destination is a global (storeLayer()==0 for the global and for any projection of it), the destination outlives every arena, so 'the stored value lives exactly as long as the destination' is false. The call-site rule cannot compensate: the argument-lifetime bound h is derived from the callee's ref-typed *parameters* (checkCallRefArgs), not from the global that is written, and a global store is not put in any effect mask (EXTC_DUMP_EFFECTS prints other=0x0 for the callee below). The same store in a callee without a home arena is rejected, which shows the intended rule.
findings.trigger: A function that (i) stores a value borrowed from one of its parameters into a global and (ii) also allocates/returns something that needs a home arena (e.g. returns a struct holding a `new` slice). Its caller passes a view into a block-local buffer.
findings.repro: c4.extc in /tmp/rev/repro: `var G: slice<u8> = "hi"`; `struct hbox { p: mut slice<u8> }`; `fn stash(p: slice<u8>) -> hbox { G = p  var b: mut slice<u8> = new u8[4]  return { p: b } }`; main calls `stash(a[..])` where `a: mut slice<u8> = new u8[64]` lives in a nested block, then allocates another 64-byte slice in the outer scope and prints G. `./build/extc c4.extc -o c4.c && gcc -fwrapv -O1 -o c4 c4.c && ./c4` -> `G = ZZZZZ...` (the released block arena was reused). The same program with `fn stash(p: slice<u8>) -> i32` (c3.extc, no home) is rejected: 'cannot store a borrowed value into something that outlives this call'. EXTC_DUMP_EFFECTS on c4 shows `stash ... fresh=1` and the emitted signature `static hbox stash(slice_u8 p, extc_arena *__extc_home)`.

findings.title: placeDepth answers 0 ('lives forever') for a place whose root is not a binding, so a local view laundered through an index/slice of a temporary is accepted where the direct store is rejected
findings.why: The fallback `root ? root->depth : 0` returns depth 0 for everything placeRoot() cannot resolve (placeRoot handles only EX_IDENT/EX_FIELD/EX_INDEX/EX_SLICE). Depth 0 means 'outside this frame, lives forever' -- the unsafe direction. exprRefDepth() routes EX_INDEX/EX_FIELD through this fallback (line 501), so `[v, v][0]` (an index of an array literal) reports depth 0 although it is a copy of a view into the current block. The companion file comment at line 244 of valDepthStructural states the rule that is broken here: under-reporting the depth 'decides how long the storage has to live', so a smaller answer is the unsafe direction. exprBorrowed() is also blind here (placeRoot()==NULL -> false), so nothing else catches it.
findings.trigger: Any store/return whose value is an element or sub-view of a temporary: `G = [v, v][0]`, `G = [v, v][0..1]`, `G = f().field`-shaped places. v is a view/ref into the current frame.
findings.repro: n1.extc vs n2.extc in /tmp/rev/repro (both store into the global `var G: slice<u8> = "hi"`): n2 is `G = v` where `v: slice<u8> = a[..]` and `a` is a block-local `[16]u8` -> rejected: 'this assignment would hold a reference to a local variable that dies first (borrowed from depth 2, but this can only hold up to depth 0)'. n1 is the same program with `G = [v, v][0]` -> accepted (0 errors), and the generated program reads the dead array (`G = ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP` after the block ended; with a sibling block that reuses the slot it is garbage).

findings.title: valTracesToParam / destIsParam compare parameter *names*, so a local that shadows a parameter makes the store publish its lifetime constraint against the wrong argument
findings.why: valTracesToParam resolves the value by its root *name* and never checks that the name denotes the parameter's Sym. Shadowing a parameter is legal and documented (examples/shadowing.extc item 4), so a nested `var s: slice<u8> = q` (q arrived from a different parameter `t`) satisfies valTracesToParam for the parameter named `s`. checkStoreEscape then accepts `b.s = s` (both destIsParam and valTracesToParam are true by name) and defers to the call site; the effect collector (check_top.c paramIndex, also by name) records the bit for the parameter named `s`; checkCallRefArgs only inspects that argument, which is the shallow one, and never looks at the deep argument that actually feeds the value. The violated invariant is the by-name mapping between source bindings and formal parameters that the whole deferral scheme depends on.
findings.trigger: Callee with two view-typed parameters, e.g. `fn stash(b: mut ref box, s: slice<u8>, t: slice<u8>)`, that copies `t` into a local and stores it through a local binding *named like the other parameter* (`{ var s: slice<u8> = q  b.s = s }`). The caller passes a shallow (static) value for `s` and a view into a block-local buffer for `t`.
findings.repro: m3.extc in /tmp/rev/repro; m2.extc is the identical program without the shadowing local. m2 is rejected: 'argument 3 of `stash` carries a reference into a deeper scope (depth 2) than the place the callee may store it (depth 1)'. m3 compiles with 0 errors (EXTC_DBG_REFARGS shows the callee's bit is `addr=0x2`, i.e. argument 2 = the shallow `s`), and running it prints `out.s = ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ` -- the caller's box points at the reused stack slot of the dead block-local `a`.

findings.title: A store into a field/element of a by-value aggregate parameter is judged against depth 0 instead of the frame, so a safe program is rejected
findings.why: storeLayer() has an explicit rule for a bare parameter: `if (sy->depth == 0 && !isGlobalSym(c, sy)) return 1;` (line 182) because 'a parameter's slot is in this frame: the argument is a copy'. That rule is not applied when the destination is projected through the parameter: placeDepth(EX_FIELD/EX_INDEX) recurses to the parameter's ident and returns sy->depth, which is 0 for every parameter, so checkStoreEscape() (line 1386) judges the store against depth 0 and rejects a value at depth 1 even though both the value and the destination die with the same frame. Struct parameters are real C by-value parameters (the emitted signature is `static void g(box b, ...)` and mutating `b` does not change the caller's object), so nothing can observe the stored view. The diagnostic even names the wrong cause ('would hold a reference to a local variable that dies first'), since no reference escapes.
findings.trigger: `struct box { s: slice<u8> }`, `fn g(b: box) { var a: [4]u8 = [...]  b.s = a[..] }`. The bare-parameter twin (`fn f(b: slice<u8>) { b = a[..] }`) is accepted, which pinpoints the asymmetry.
findings.repro: a2b.extc in /tmp/rev/repro holds both functions: `f` (bare `slice<u8>` parameter, store to the binding) compiles, `g` (store to `b.s`) is rejected at line 11: 'this assignment would hold a reference to a local variable that dies first (borrowed from depth 1, but this can only hold up to depth 0)'. a3.extc shows the by-value semantics: `./build/extc a3.extc -o a3.c && gcc -fwrapv -O1 -o a3 a3.c && ./a3` prints `v=1 s=hi` after `set(b, a[..])` assigned `b.v = 7` and `b.s = src` inside the callee.

findings.title: A global whose annotated type is a nullable reference cannot be initialized with `null`: the annotation is not used as context for the initializer
findings.why: The global's declared type (g->ann, resolved at line 4398) is never adopted as the context of the initializer, unlike local declarations, so EX_NULL sees no context and checkExprInner() (check_expr.c:1237) reports '`null` here does not know which `?ref T` it is' -- the very diagnostic that recommends the syntax `var p: ?ref node = null` being rejected here. The type is only compared afterwards via checkAssignable. Semantically the program is a plain C static initializer of a nullable pointer, and the same declaration inside a function body is accepted. (This finding is outside the assigned range read; it is the global-initializer half of the same depth-0 story and is reported for routing.)
findings.trigger: Module-level `var G: ?ref i32 = null` (or any `?ref T` global with a `null` initializer), as opposed to the same declaration inside a function.
findings.repro: h2.extc in /tmp/rev/repro: `var B: ?ref i32 = null` -> `./build/extc h2.extc -o h2.c` reports 'h2.extc:1:1: error: `null` here does not know which `?ref T` it is'. The identical declaration inside a function (a4.extc) compiles. `var D: slice<u8> = "hi"` (same file, non-null constant) is accepted, so the failure is specific to the context-handed `null`.

coverage_notes: Read all of src/check_escape.c lines 1-1290 in order (plus 1291-2571 for callers/helpers and the whole file's helper use), and cross-read the callees/callers that these functions depend on: checkCallRefArgs / computeEffectsTransitive / stmtStoresThroughDeref / paramIndex / fieldDepthEntry / refreshRootDepth / noteFieldDepthWrite / noteWholeValueDepthWrite (check_top.c), typeContainsRef / typeContainsRefAt / placeRoot / identBindOf / Sym.refDepth initialization (check_lookup.c, check.c), the declaration, assignment and return paths in check_stmt.c, the level replay (check_top.c:6040-6110), the EX_NEW arenaLevel assignment (check_expr.c:2313-2341), tsub/mentionsParam (check.c), and the manual's safety chapter. Checked as correct: every ExprKind has a case in exprRefDepth/valDepthStructural (no missing kind), typeContainsRef really does recurse into struct fields and enum payloads (so valDepthStructural's comment at 191-194 and typeCannotCarryRef are not a hole), promoteInto2's hop cap (32) and originOf's cap really do break binding cycles (k2.extc terminates), the 'tighten only when every child succeeded' discipline is respected in the STRUCTLIT/ARRAYLIT/ENUMVAL cases, arenaDepthOf treats 0/undecided as depth 0 only for sites that already have a level assigned, the recordStore dedup cannot drop a *sharper* (smaller) level, recheckLevelRejections only feeds diagnostics, and rule A's max(argument depth) bound is otherwise upheld (the free-generic-function version of the borrowed-store test is still caught at the call site: g3.extc, 'argument 2 ... depth 2 ... depth 1'). Not reproduced despite trying: a crash or hang in this pass (a 600-iteration mutation fuzz run found only the intended SIGSEGV of tests/heap/afterclose.extc), and a free-generic `recordRefCheck` no-op (the call-site content rule catches it). Every finding above has a compiling, running repro under /tmp/rev/repro.
